title: CodeMother answers a chart verb on the bus
intention: CodeMother answers a chart verb on the bus: one request floors or writes one of her eight chart stages (orient through validate, and verdict) and answers the packet or the berth, so a builder reaches the chart chain through her public interface instead of importing her machines.
why: Measured 2026-11-10: CodeMother's verbs (outline 9.6, cairn/devices/codemother/shim.py) write no chart stage, so the /chart skill's instructions and CC's chart and verdict helpers import her machines; cairn/devices/cc/proofs/test_cc_proofs_reach_no_other_device.py reds those imports under RULE 1.
traces_to: RULE 1 (a device is reached through its public interface); outline 9.3.2, 9.3.4, 9.6 and Q#81.
how: Add 'chart' to CodeMotherShim.declared_verbs, dispatching through a module-level CHART_STAGES table (stage -> (floor function, write function)); the shim takes chart_dir for its writes; refusals ride back named. Outline 9.6 and her charter name the verb. Red-first proof drives the handler directly.

clauses.claim: CHART_STAGES in the shim maps each of the eight stage names to that stage machine's own floor and write functions (verdict has a writer and no floor)
the chart verb with op floor and stage orient returns orient.floor_packet's packet for the request and writes nothing
the chart verb with op write and stage orient writes the packet under the shim's chart dir and answers accepted with that berth on disk
an unknown stage, an unknown op, or a stage with no floor asked to floor is refused, accepted False, naming the valid choices, and nothing is written
a writer that raises comes back accepted False with the error's type and text, and nothing is written
outline 9.6 and CodeMother's charter name the chart verb

decisions.text: D1: cairn/devices/codemother/shim.py: a module-level CHART_STAGES dict, stage -> (floor or None, writer), importing each stage module lazily inside a function chart_stages(); CodeMotherShim.__init__ takes chart_dir=None; declared_verbs gains 'chart': self._handle_chart. chart: body {stage, op, input}; stage is one of orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict; op floor calls the stage's floor (orient.floor_packet(request), constrain_floor(intent_ref), survey_floor, decompose_floor, triage_floor, hypothesize_floor, validate_floor) and returns its packet without writing; op write calls the stage's writer (write_packet, write_constrain, ..., write_verdict) with the shim's chart instance dir and returns the berth. Every refusal is {accepted: False, verb: chart, device: codemother, reason}} naming the choices; an exception from a stage function is caught and returned the same way with its type and text (Law 7).

D2: cairn/devices/codemother/intention+why.json names the chart verb in its public interface through the artifact door; press_office/CairnComponentOutline.txt 9.6's VERBS line gains chart once Q#81 is answered yes (the answer's own wording lands there).

D3: the proof cairn/devices/codemother/proofs/test_codemother_answers_a_chart_verb.py, red-first, one tooth per clause, PROVES 1-6; it builds CodeMotherShim(chart_dir=<a scratch dir>) and calls declared_verbs()['chart'] with envelopes, never the bus; guarded imports and the house runner.

measured.saw: nine verbs, none writes a stage; 14 imports in SKILL.md, 7 in chart_ticket.py, 1 in verdict_ticket.py
measured.how: read cairn/devices/codemother/shim.py declared_verbs and grep of skills/chart/SKILL.md, cairn/devices/cc/scripts/chart_ticket.py, cairn/devices/cc/scripts/verdict_ticket.py for codemother imports
